To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

response based methods have been widely developed for road profile reconstruction and pothole detection, but there is a lack of comprehensive systems for road roughness index and road surface condition assessment.

response based methods have the potential to be the next generation road surface condition evaluation system, but further research is needed in terms of robustness of algorithms, data collection and data fusion.
the state of the road profile reconstruction is promising, but the road roughness index reconstruction and pothole detection are still at an early stage.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects of road condition measurement: (1) the development of algorithms and systems that are independent on the vehicle dynamics, (2) the development of a novel and comprehensive road condition assessment method and (3) the integration of existing methods and systems to provide a comprehensive road condition assessment platform for road maintenance and management.

the following aspects: 1) the state-of-the-art response based methods for road surface condition evaluation; 2) the advantages and disadvantages of each technique and system; 3) the key focus areas of research and development in the future.
the key challenges in response based road surface condition evaluation and the future research directions are also proposed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single method that can be used to replace the existing road condition assessment methods.
the current research in response based methods is mainly focusing on the development of algorithms and systems for road profile reconstruction and pothole detection.
there is no single best method for measuring road surface conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
response based methods are increasingly used to reconstruct/estimate the road profile and detect anomalies.
the response based methods are still at a relatively early stage and there are opportunities for further research.
there is a clear gap between road profile estimation and roughness estimation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the road profile reconstruction is more accurate, the pothole detection is more efficient and road roughness estimation is more reliable when compared with the other two methods.
the current research in the area of response based methods for road surface irregularity is still in its infancy and there is a lot of room for future development.
the road roughness estimation is a complex problem that requires a holistic approach to be solved.
